title: Future time
subtitle: Will, be going to, present tenses for the future, future perfect, time clauses, prepositions of time and place

theory.title: will / won't and be going to

blocks.text: There is sometimes little difference in meaning between **will** and **be going to**. It is often just a matter of formality. **Will** is generally more formal than **be going to**.

rows.example: The website **will** come online next week. (more formal) · The website's **going to** come online next week. (more informal)

rows.use: Predictions not based on present evidence
rows.example: In the future, everyone **will** have their own flying car. (more formal) · In the future, everyone **is going to** have their own flying car. (more informal)

rows.use: Decisions made at the moment of speaking
rows.example: I've decided! I **won't** get a new DVD player just yet. (emphasising the decision) · I've decided! I'm **not going to** get a new DVD player just yet. (emphasising the intention)

blocks.intro: Sometimes it is more appropriate to use **will** rather than **be going to**.
items: Offers and suggestions: I'll **help** you with your physics homework, if you like.
Requests: **Will** you help me with my physics homework?
Most first conditional sentences: If we get a computer, we'll **be** able to surf the Internet.

blocks.text: With offers and suggestions in the question form, we do not use **will** with **I** and **we**. We use **shall**.
blocks.note: **Shall** I help you with your physics homework? (not *Will I help you …*)

blocks.intro: Sometimes it is more appropriate to use **be going to** rather than **will**.
items: Plans and intentions (which you already have when you speak): I'm **going to be** a famous doctor one day!
Predictions based on present evidence: It sounds like the plane's **going to take off** in a few minutes.

theory.title: Present continuous and present simple for the future

rows.use: Present continuous · arrangements made before the moment of speaking
rows.example: **Are** they **installing** the new computers next week?

rows.use: Present simple · timetables, arrangements and fixed events (which the speaker cannot change)
rows.example: The bus to the science museum **leaves** at 8 o'clock tomorrow morning.

rows.use: Present simple · after **if** in first conditional and zero conditional sentences
rows.example: If technology **continues** to advance so quickly, what **will** life be like in a hundred years?

rows.use: Present simple · after certain time expressions
rows.example: We'll find out as soon as we **get** to the lab.

rows.use: Future perfect simple · **will/won't + have + past participle** · actions completed between now and a point in the future
rows.example: I'll **have finished** my chemistry homework by the time you come home.

rows.use: Future continuous · **will/won't + be + -ing** · actions in progress at a point in the future
rows.example: This time next week, I'll **be taking** my biology exam.

rows.use: Future continuous · habits or repeated actions in the future
rows.example: In the future, we'll all **be flying** around using jet-packs.

rows.use: Future perfect continuous · **will/won't + have been + -ing** · actions in progress up to a point in the future
rows.example: At seven o'clock, I'll **have been doing** my chemistry homework for three hours!

blocks.text: In time clauses, we do not use **will** or **be going to** immediately after some time words and phrases. We use a present tense (present simple, present continuous or present perfect) to talk about the future.

rows.example: It'll be wonderful **when** scientists **find / have found** a cure for cancer.
Let me know **as soon as** your new computer **arrives / has arrived**.
It'll be several years **before** we **send / have sent** a manned mission to Mars.
Let's go for a pizza **after** we **go / have been** to the natural history museum.
The rocket won't be launched **until** they **do / have done** a final check.
Think of me **while** you **travel / are travelling** to the Moon!
We'll stop for petrol **once** we **pass / have passed** Cambridge.

Speakers of American English do not always use **on** before days of the week: US *We've got a biology test Monday.* · UK *We've got a biology test on Monday.*
Speakers of American English often say **Monday through Friday**: US *I'm going to be on a field trip Monday through Friday.* · UK *I'm going to be on a field trip from Monday to Friday.*

exercises.title: A · Tick or correct
exercises.instruction: If the word or phrase in bold is correct, write it again. If it is incorrect, rewrite it correctly, including all possibilities.

items.prompt: The universe **is going to** continue to expand for billions of years.
Look out! You **will** hit the car in front!
**I'm going to** do the washing-up tonight, if you like.
Do you think that, in the future, people **will live** to be hundreds of years old?
acceptedAnswers: will live / are going to live

items.prompt: **Will I** carry some of those bags for you, or can you manage?
I know! **I'm going to** have a barbecue on my birthday!
**Are you going to** just hold this door open for me for a minute? Thanks a lot!
We've decided we **will try** that new restaurant after the play tomorrow night.
**We're going to** fly to Jamaica in the summer.
**Shall we** invite Tony and Tim round tonight?
**Are we going to** invite Tony and Tim round tonight?
**Will you go** to Jason's party next Saturday?

exercises.title: B · Circle the correct phrase
exercises.instruction: Select the form that fits. If both forms are possible, choose the option that says both.

items.prompt: ___ miss the train, are we?

acceptedAnswers: both: We aren't / We're not going to

items.prompt: I think ___ really badly in the English test tomorrow.
options: both: I'm going to do / I'm doing

items.prompt: Josh ___ a song in the school talent contest next week.

acceptedAnswers: both: is going to sing / is singing

items.prompt: I'm going to ___ a big yacht if I can when I'm older.
Sports Day ___ held on the last day of term.
options: both: is going to be / is being
acceptedAnswers: both: is going to be / is being

items.prompt: ___ the concert on Thursday last more than two hours?
___ the music awards live tomorrow night?
options: both: Are they going to broadcast / Will they broadcast
acceptedAnswers: both: Are they going to broadcast / Will they broadcast

items.prompt: ___ the music awards live tomorrow night?

items.prompt: According to the timetable, the train for Oxford ___ at 10.15.

exercises.title: E · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Write between two and five words.

items.prompt:
We'll get home and then we'll have something to eat. **got**
We'll have something to eat ___ home.

I'll finish marking the exams and then I'll tell you your results. **soon**
I'll tell you your results ___ marking the exams.
acceptedAnswers: as soon as I have finished

items.prompt:
You'll be travelling across the Sahara next week so remember to wear lots of sunscreen! **while**
Remember to wear lots of sunscreen ___ across the Sahara next week!

They'll show Titan at the cinema and then they'll release the DVD. **before**
They won't release the DVD ___ at the cinema.

My science exam starts at ten tomorrow morning. **taking**
At ten past ten tomorrow ___ my science exam.

Let's have supper ___ the space documentary.

By lunchtime, ___ all the invitations.

I won't give you a test ___ some revision.

We'll have moved into our new house ___ you visit us.

We'll get some more information and then we'll make a decision. **once**
Let's make a decision ___ got some more information.

exercises.title: F · Watkins Tours
exercises.instruction: Read the timetable and write a question for each answer given. Example: What time does the coach leave Plymouth? — It leaves at 5.30 am.

items.prompt: He'll be driving the coach to Penzance.
acceptedAnswers: Who will be driving the coach to Penzance?
Who'll be driving the coach to Penzance?

items.prompt: It'll arrive at 8.15 am.
acceptedAnswers: What time will the coach arrive in Penzance?
When will it arrive in Penzance?

items.prompt: It's going to set sail at 9.15 am.
acceptedAnswers: What time is the ferry going to set sail?
When is the ferry going to leave?
What time is it going to set sail?

items.prompt: It will have been sailing for two hours.
acceptedAnswers: How long will it have been sailing?
How long will the ferry have been sailing?

items.prompt: They will just have arrived in St Mary's.
acceptedAnswers: Where will they have arrived at 12.00 noon?
Where will they just have arrived?

items.prompt: They'll be walking round the town.
acceptedAnswers: What will they be doing from 12 to 1.30 pm?
What will they be doing at lunchtime?

items.prompt: They'll be having a picnic lunch.
acceptedAnswers: What will they be doing from 1.30 to 2.30 pm?
When will they be having a picnic lunch?

items.prompt: They'll be leaving the beach at 4 pm.
acceptedAnswers: What time will they be leaving the beach?
When will they be leaving the beach?

items.prompt: They'll have just finished a boat trip round the island.
acceptedAnswers: What will they have just finished at 4 pm?
What will they have just finished?

items.prompt: It's leaving at 4.30 pm.
acceptedAnswers: What time is the ferry leaving?

items.prompt: They get back at 10.15 pm.

When do they get back to Plymouth?
